teaser.text: IHG Hotels & Resorts sells hotel owners a recognised brand and a ready-made way to attract guests, while owning very few hotels itself. Its business is therefore less about buildings than about turning brands, bookings and loyalty into fees.

blocks.heading: Where could IHG's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast points to moderate gains, but the possible outcomes remain unusually wide. The weighted price is $175.65 by October 2027, a 6% return including dividends. It reaches $196.21 by October 2028, a 19% return. By October 2029, it reaches $215.55, a 32% return.
At the final date, the modeled range runs from $97.19 to $347.53. The base case receives the largest probability, at 55%. The bear case has 25%, while the bull case has 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for IHG?

paragraphs.text: The view would move bearward during 2027–2028 if RevPAR and underlying fee revenue slow, especially in Greater China. It would weaken further through 2029 if signed rooms fail to open, owner financing constraints raise support costs, or free cash flow cannot sustain buybacks while leverage remains elevated.

blocks.heading: How much cash does IHG really make?

paragraphs.text: Net income was $758 million in 2025, while cash from operations was $898 million. Capital spending was $197 million and lease payments were $30 million. That produced free cash flow of $671 million. Deducting $72 million of stock pay gives a narrower “real free cash flow” of $599 million. This is an analytical allowance for dilution, not a second cash payment.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for IHG today?

paragraphs.text: P/E, or price-to-earnings, shows what investors pay for each dollar of earnings per share. Trailing P/E uses the last twelve months; forward P/E uses the next twelve months. Basic EPS follows accounting profit, while adjusted EPS removes items IHG considers less representative. The denominator therefore matters. A low free-cash-flow yield also means that future growth must justify the price, especially because key money—cash paid to win hotel contracts—helps acquire future fees but still consumes cash.

dividend.title: IHG dividend: cash coverage and outlook
dividend.meta_description: IHG pays a growing dividend, but recent shareholder payouts exceeded free cash flow and future payments depend on cash conversion.
dividend.opening: IHG declared an interim dividend of 64.5¢, and its forecast dividends are $1.419 in 2027, $1.561 in 2028, and $1.717 in 2029. In 2025, IHG generated $671m of free cash flow, paid $270m in dividends and spent $897m on buybacks, so shareholder payouts exceeded free cash flow.
dividend.closing: The full memo also covers IHG’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does IHG pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends also distinguish the cases. The declared interim dividend is 64.5¢, and the recent annual increase has been 10%. Base dividends are $1.419 in 2027 and $1.561 in 2028. They reach $1.717 in 2029. The bear case holds dividends at $1.355 after the first period, while the bull case reaches $2.043 through faster growth. The bear reflects the 2020 withdrawal of a recommended final dividend; the base follows the recent record.

blocks.heading: Does IHG’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: From 2022 onwards, shareholder payments exceeded free cash flow every year. In 2025, IHG generated $671m of free cash flow. It paid $270m in dividends and spent $897m on buybacks. That created a $496m shortfall before other uses and sources of cash.

Net income was $758 million in 2025, while cash from operations was $898 million. Capital spending was $197 million and lease payments were $30 million. That produced free cash flow of $671 million. Deducting $72 million of stock pay gives a narrower “real free cash flow” of $599 million. This is an analytical allowance for dilution, not a second cash payment.

paragraphs.text: Management targets adjusted EPS growth of 12–15% a year across 2026–2027. It targets annual fee-margin expansion of 100–150 basis points. Adjusted earnings should convert fully into adjusted free cash flow on average across 2026–2027, with net debt to adjusted EBITDA targeted at 2.5–3.0 times. Annual key money—funds that may support hotel openings or renovations—and maintenance CapEx is $200–250 million for 2026–2027. Gross CapEx is expected to average $350 million a year.
